newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Continuing upward pressure seen on Australian wool.
newsitem.headline: Continuing upward pressure seen on Australian wool.

text.p: The net effect of supply and demand factors is expected to place continued upward pressure on wool prices this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said.
Wesfarmers said this week's small offering will again stimulate competition as buyers try to fill orders. Sales are in Sydney, Adelaude and Fremantle with 77,000 bales on offer.
"The factors which drove the price rises last week are expected to remain in force this week and cause further market gains," Wesfarmers said in a market preview.
The eastern market indicator rose 12 cents to a 22-month high of 726 cents a kg clean last week.
Wesfarmers said the most important factor supporting this upward trend is that supply is limited.

Other factors are an encouraging flow of new orders, including business from China at levels close to the market, and dramatic falls in the Australian dollar which have made the price of wool substantially cheaper for overseas buyers and will continue to stimulate orders.
As well, strength in wool futures, particularly in distant months, is a positive sign and an indicator of trade confidence.
